questions.question: A can finish a work in 12 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. If they work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: A's 1 day work = 1/12. B's 1 day work = 1/15. Combined 1 day work = 1/12 + 1/15 = (5+4)/60 = 9/60 = 3/20. Total time = 20/3 = 6.66 days.

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 8 days, which A alone can do in 12 days. In how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.explanation: B's 1 day work = (1/8) - (1/12) = (3 - 2)/24 = 1/24. Therefore, B alone can complete the work in 24 days.

questions.question: A train running at a speed of 60 km/hr crosses a pole in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train in meters?
questions.explanation: Speed in m/s = 60 * (5/18) = 50/3 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = (50/3) * 9 = 150 meters.

questions.question: An article is bought for $400 and sold for $500. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price = 500 - 400 = 100. Profit % = (100 / 400) * 100 = 25%.
